record.paper_title: Some Open Problems on Multiple Ergodic Averages
record.original_question: If p1, ..., pℓ are integer-valued generalized polynomials and T1, ..., Tℓ are commuting measure-preserving transformations, do the averages (1/N) Σ_{n=1}^N T1^{p1(n)}f1 · ... · Tℓ^{pℓ(n)}fℓ always converge in L^2?

evidence.quote: Problem 14. Let p1, . . . , p` be integer valued generalized polynomials. Show that the averages (1/N) ΣN n=1 T1^p1(n) f1 · · · T`^p`(n) f` converge in the mean as N → ∞.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $(X,\mathcal{B},\mu)$ be a probability space, and let $T_1,\ldots,T_\ell:X\to X$ be invertible commuting measure-preserving transformations. A function $p:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{Z}$ is called a (integer-valued) generalized polynomial if it can be obtained from the identity function and constants by finitely many applications of addition, multiplication, and the floor function $\lfloor\cdot\rfloor$, and takes integer values on $\mathbb{N}$. Examples include $\lfloor n\sqrt{2}\rfloor\lfloor n\sqrt{3}\rfloor$ and $\lfloor n^2\alpha\rfloor + n^3$.

Let $p_1,\ldots,p_\ell$ be integer-valued generalized polynomials, and let $f_1,\ldots,f_\ell\in L^\infty(X,\mu)$. Determine whether the multiple ergodic averages
$$\frac{1}{N}\sum_{n=1}^{N}\bigl(T_1^{p_1(n)}f_1\bigr)\bigl(T_2^{p_2(n)}f_2\bigr)\cdots\bigl(T_\ell^{p_\ell(n)}f_\ell\bigr)$$
converge in $L^2(X,\mu)$ as $N\to\infty$.
artifact.status_search_result: Walsh's 2012 theorem (Annals of Math.) establishes $L^2$-norm convergence of multiple ergodic averages along ordinary polynomial iterates for nilpotent (in particular commuting) groups of measure-preserving transformations, but his methods do not directly cover iterates given by generalized polynomials (which involve the floor function). Convergence results for generalized polynomial iterates are known only in restricted settings (e.g., single transformation, or special classes of generalized polynomials), and the general commuting case appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Norm convergence of nilpotent ergodic averages
status_evidence.snippet: Walsh proved that multiple polynomial ergodic averages arising from nilpotent groups of measure preserving transformations always converge in the L^2 norm.
status_evidence.claim: Walsh's theorem covers ordinary polynomial iterates (not generalized polynomials) for commuting/nilpotent transformations.

status_evidence.title: Some Open Problems on Multiple Ergodic Averages (Frantzikinakis)
status_evidence.snippet: Problem 14. Let p1,...,p_l be integer valued generalized polynomials. Show that the averages (1/N) sum T1^{p1(n)} f1 ... T_l^{p_l(n)} f_l converge in the mean as N -> infinity.
status_evidence.claim: The convergence problem for generalized polynomial iterates with commuting transformations is listed as an open problem.
